title: Low-Stretching Cryptographic Hash Functions for Password Storage
pattern: Protecting client passwords by running them through standard, fast cryptographic hashing algorithms (like MD5, SHA-1, or SHA-256) instead of slow, memory-hard key derivation algorithms.
why_bad: Fast hash functions are highly optimized for CPU execution speeds. Attackers who exfiltrate the password database can perform brute-force dictionary attacks at rates of billions of guesses per second using low-cost custom hardware, trivially recovering user credentials.
detection: The invocation of single-round MD5 or SHA hashing algorithms inside credential processing modules.
fix: Utilize salted key derivation functions specifically designed for password stretching, such as `Argon2`, `scrypt`, or `bcrypt`, to make brute-force attacks computationally infeasible.
source: `Heather Adkins et al. - Building Secure and Reliable Systems (2020)`, Ch 18, p. 434.
